validity.researcher_notes: Two spec discrepancies surfaced from the same single interview source this pass, both disclosed on their respective fills[] REFS_ADDED records (staged at the GEM-recorded values, not overridden) and consolidated here as one spec concern. (1) LENGTH: source's ~600 km is a rounded, colloquial figure from a retrospective interview, not a technical spec sheet -- a ~21% gap from GEM's 763 km is material and worth checking against an engineering-grade source (e.g. a Gazprom Transgaz Tomsk technical passport or GIS trace), but not confident enough on this evidence alone to recommend replacing GEM's number. (2) START: the 1-year gap (1988 vs 1989) is plausibly explained by 'first gas physically reached the region' (1988, the interview's framing) vs. a later formal in-service/commissioning date (1989, GEM's convention elsewhere) -- but this pass could not independently confirm which milestone GEM's 1989 reflects, so it is flagged rather than resolved. Both left as open items for a future targeted-source pass, not urgent enough to escalate beyond this validity record given the lean-pass budget.
